To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vicilin like storage protein of cocoa consists of three sub units with apparent molecular masses between 15 and 47 kDa and that these sub units are derived from a single precursor with a molecular mass of 66 kDa.

the cocoa vicillin like globulin is encoded by a gene that is highly conserved in all species of the genus Theobroma and is composed of three subunits, which are derived by post translational modifications of a common precursor.

The precursor of the vicilin-like globulin of cocoa seeds is encoded by a gene that is expressed in all tissues of the seed, including the cotyledon and the endosperm, but not the testa and the seed coat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the origin of cocoa specific aroma precursions.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of cocoa specific flavour formation during fermentation.
the elucidation of the subunit composition of the vicilin storage protein and the identification of the precursor regions of the cocoa specific aroma precursor peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cocoa vicilin is a single polypeptide chain of 660 amino acids (66 kDa) and that the three subunits are generated by proteolytic cleavage of this precursor.
the vicilin like seed storage protein of cocoa is a single gene product, which is encoded by a gene of 2019 nucleotides, which is interrupted by three introns.
the vicilin like protein of cocoa seeds consists of three subunit species, which are encoded by a single common precursor sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vicilin of cocoa seeds is a single gene encoded protein, consisting of three subunits, which are derived post translationally by proteolysis.
the vicilin like storage protein of cocoa seed is composed of three subunits of 47 kD, 31 kD and 15 kD.

the vicilin like storage protein of the cocoa seed is encoded by a gene that is highly conserved in all legumes and that the subunit heterogeneity is caused by post translational modifications of the precursor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cocoa specific aroma precursers are generated by proteolysis from the vicilin like storage protein.

the cocoa vicilins, which have not yet been described in detail, are not encoded by multiple genes, but by a single gene, and that the observed heterogeneity of the subunits is caused by statistical post translational modification.
